core_claim: AFM 3 Core Advanced is a 20B sparse on-device model that activates 1-4B parameters and stores the full model in NAND while loading selected experts into DRAM.
memory_impact: Cuts active DRAM footprint for on-device inference; shifts some demand from DRAM to NAND/flash plus software routing.
industry_readthrough: Bearish for simple DRAM-capacity assumptions in edge AI; not a replacement for HBM in frontier training or high-throughput cloud inference.

paper_or_source: Apple Intelligence Foundation Language Models Tech Report 2025
core_claim: Apple's on-device model uses KV-cache sharing and 2-bit quantization-aware training; server model uses PT-MoE with global-local attention.
memory_impact: Reduces on-device memory and latency; confirms production models are moving toward aggressive compression.
industry_readthrough: Shows consumer AI will not map linearly to DRAM/HBM GB demand; favors efficient local models and adapters.

paper_or_source: Apple On-Device and Server Foundation Models
core_claim: Apple uses activation/embedding quantization, efficient KV-cache updates, and dynamically swapped adapters of tens of MB.
memory_impact: Keeps model specialization cheap without loading many full models.
industry_readthrough: Supports adapter/LoRA demand rather than massive on-device base-model memory.

core_claim: Google Research reports at least 6x KV-cache memory reduction and up to 8x speedup with near-zero loss via online vector quantization.
memory_impact: Strongly reduces long-context inference KV footprint and attention memory traffic.
industry_readthrough: Medium-term bearish for HBM capacity per token; may be bullish for total tokens served through Jevons effect.

core_claim: ICLR 2026 poster reports quality-neutral KV quantization at 3.5 bits per channel and marginal degradation at 2.5 bits.
memory_impact: Validates practical sub-4-bit KV cache as a serious systems path.
industry_readthrough: Raises risk that HBM demand growth migrates from capacity to bandwidth/utilization.

core_claim: KIVI proposes tuning-free 2-bit asymmetric KV-cache quantization for LLMs.
memory_impact: Reduces KV capacity pressure for long-context inference.
industry_readthrough: Earlier proof that KV cache can be compressed aggressively; industry impact depends on serving integration.

core_claim: KVQuant compresses activations dynamically and reports large KV memory savings for long contexts.
memory_impact: Allows larger batch size or context length under same memory budget.
industry_readthrough: Bearish for raw GB-per-token but bullish for long-context productization.

core_claim: XQuant caches low-bit layer inputs and rematerializes K/V, trading compute for lower memory traffic.
memory_impact: Cuts stored cache and shifts burden to recompute.
industry_readthrough: Potentially reduces HBM capacity need but increases compute; net demand depends on power economics.

core_claim: System-aware 4-bit KV-cache quantization with fused rotation-quantization kernel and negligible serving overhead.
memory_impact: Makes KV compression closer to production-ready under real serving constraints.
industry_readthrough: More bearish for naive HBM demand models than academic-only compression.

core_claim: Fine-grained KV retrieval matches full KV using 11% cache budget on long-context tasks.
memory_impact: Evicts/retrieves useful cache instead of storing everything hot.
industry_readthrough: Useful for agentic long-context workloads; can reduce peak memory at cost of retrieval complexity.

core_claim: PagedAttention manages KV cache with paging to improve memory utilization and throughput.
memory_impact: Reduces memory fragmentation and improves GPU utilization without changing model architecture.
industry_readthrough: Bullish for inference volume, mildly bearish for wasted HBM demand.

core_claim: FlashAttention-3 improves attention by reducing HBM IO and using Hopper asynchronous features and low precision.
memory_impact: Reduces bandwidth waste and improves effective HBM utilization.
industry_readthrough: Does not eliminate HBM need; raises tokens per GPU and can expand demand.

core_claim: DeepSeek-V3 uses Multi-head Latent Attention and MoE to improve inference efficiency and training economics.
memory_impact: MLA compresses cached KV states; MoE reduces active compute per token.
industry_readthrough: Important architectural proof that frontier-quality models can reduce KV cache and active parameters.

core_claim: Multi-head Latent Attention can be transplanted to existing MHA models while reducing KV cache size.
memory_impact: Shows MLA-style KV compression may spread beyond DeepSeek-native models.
industry_readthrough: Bearish for full-MHA memory assumptions if conversion quality holds.

core_claim: Hybrid linear attention reports up to 75% KV-cache reduction and up to 6x decoding throughput for 1M context.
memory_impact: Moves part of sequence memory from unbounded KV cache to compact recurrent state.
industry_readthrough: Potentially material if adopted in frontier and agent models; still needs scale validation.

core_claim: Lightning attention plus MoE supports million-token context at affordable cost.
memory_impact: Reduces long-context memory/computation scaling versus pure full attention.
industry_readthrough: Points to hybrid attention becoming mainstream for long context.

core_claim: Open-weight reasoning model combines MoE with lightning attention and 1M native context.
memory_impact: Connects efficient attention to test-time compute and reasoning workloads.
industry_readthrough: If reasoning demand grows, efficiency may enable more inference rather than less memory spend.

core_claim: Selective state-space models scale linearly in sequence length and report faster inference than Transformers.
memory_impact: Avoids unbounded KV cache but has tradeoffs in content-based recall.
industry_readthrough: Long-term threat to attention KV cache; near-term likely hybrid rather than full replacement.

core_claim: Generalized SSM design links attention and state-space models; hybrid SSM-attention can improve efficiency.
memory_impact: Supports mixed architecture design with fewer attention layers.
industry_readthrough: Favors architectures that reduce but do not eliminate HBM pressure.

core_claim: Gated DeltaNet improves Mamba2/DeltaNet style linear attention with hardware-efficient training.
memory_impact: Replaces some attention cache with recurrent state.
industry_readthrough: Important building block for Kimi/Qwen-like hybrids.

core_claim: Gated DeltaNet-2 uses fixed-size recurrent state for constant-memory decoding and improves long-context retrieval.
memory_impact: Directly attacks unbounded cache growth in long-context inference.
industry_readthrough: If validated at larger scale, this is structurally bearish for KV-cache-driven HBM capacity demand.

core_claim: Qualcomm says HBC fuses memory and compute dies, avoids HBM tax, and provides 7.4 PB/s effective bandwidth per rack for AI250.
memory_impact: Alternative to HBM for disaggregated inference; uses near-memory compute and LPDDR capacity.
industry_readthrough: Potential long-term competitive threat to HBM in inference, but unproven at NVIDIA-scale software and workload breadth.

core_claim: SK hynix completed HBM4 development and prepared mass production for high-performance AI memory.
memory_impact: Expands HBM supply and bandwidth roadmap.
industry_readthrough: Bullish for HBM unit growth, but supply ramp can pressure pricing if software efficiency also improves.

core_claim: Samsung says HBM sales can more than triple in 2026 and HBM4E/custom HBM samples follow.
memory_impact: Expands HBM4 supply and custom memory roadmap.
industry_readthrough: Supply response is accelerating; price supercycle risk rises if demand elasticity weakens.

core_claim: NVFP4 targets efficient low-precision inference with large memory-budget benefits for test-time scaling.
memory_impact: Cuts model weight footprint and memory bandwidth per operation.
industry_readthrough: Bullish for inference demand and tokens served; reduces GB per model copy.
